_transcription: ENGLISH PAGES USED: idx 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14. Full page map, all 16 accounted for and the English ones confirmed at full size: idx0 = bilingual cover (Series PPQQC/2, SET-1, Q.P. Code 30/2/1, 'Mathematics (Standard) - Theory', 2 hours, 40 marks, 16 printed pages); idx1 = HINDI instructions + Q1-2; idx2 = ENGLISH General Instructions + Q1-2; idx3 = HINDI Q3-4; idx4 = ENGLISH Q3-4; idx5 = HINDI Q5-8; idx6 = ENGLISH Q5-8; idx7 = HINDI Q9-10; idx8 = ENGLISH Q9-10; idx9 = HINDI Q11-12; idx10 = ENGLISH Q11-12; idx11 = HINDI Q13; idx12 = ENGLISH Q13; idx13 = HINDI Q14; idx14 = ENGLISH Q14; idx15 = BLANK apart from the QR code, an asterisk and the footer. Each odd page is the Hindi of the page after it; every odd page opens with Hindi and no English sits at the top of any odd page; no parity inversion. STRUCTURE (printed General Instructions, idx2): 14 questions, Section A Q1-6 @2, Section B Q7-10 @3, Section C Q11-14 @4 with two case-study questions (Q13 'Case Study - 1', Q14 'Case Study - 2'). 12 + 12 + 16 = 40, matching term2_m10 exactly. No MCQs: every row is subjective, no keys. INTERNAL CHOICE: the instructions print counts, two in Section A, one in B, one in C; found Q2, Q4, Q9, Q12, each printed (a) / OR / (b) and each confirmed against the marking scheme, which reprints both branches with an 'Or' between them. No OR in either case study. 20 rows = 14 questions + 4 OR alternatives + 2 extra case-study parts. CASE-STUDY LABELS: the paper prints the parts as (1) and (2), not (i)/(ii); refs are Q13i/Q13ii and Q14i/Q14ii, questionNumber keeps the printed '13 (1)' etc. Part marks as printed: Q13 2 + 2, Q14 3 + 1. Q13's passage carries a printed title, 'Kite Festival', kept as the first line of the context. Class intervals keep the printed spaced dashes (0 – 15); Q10's table prints them unspaced (130-135) and is kept so. No decimal points appear in any question. Opener of series 30/2: nothing skipped.

Kite Festival

Kite festival is celebrated in many countries at different times of the year. In India, every year \(14^{\text{th}}\) January is celebrated as International Kite Day. On this day many people visit India and participate in the festival by flying various kinds of kites.

The picture given below, shows three kites flying together.

In Fig. 5, the angles of elevation of two kites (Points A and B) from the hands of a man (Point C) are found to be \(30^\circ\) and \(60^\circ\) respectively. Taking AD = 50 m and BE = 60 m, find
questions.stem: the lengths of strings used (take them straight) for kites A and B as shown in the figure.
